title: Framework vs .NET: the differences
sub: A cheat sheet and a migration plan
cards/0/body:
Where it runs: Framework on Windows; .NET on Windows, Linux, macOS.
Installation: Framework is one per system, updated in place; .NET versions sit side by side or ship with the app.
Evolution: Framework gets fixes only; .NET gets a new version every year.
Speed: .NET is noticeably faster.
cards/1/body: An old .csproj is hundreds of lines listing every file, plus packages.config. The new SDK style is a few lines: files are picked up automatically, and packages come via PackageReference.
cards/2/q: Which line gives away that this project targets .NET Framework?
cards/2/explain: SDK style works for Framework too. TargetFramework sets the target.
cards/4/body:
1. Convert projects to SDK style.
2. Move shared code into a netstandard2.0 library that works on both sides.
3. Find incompatible APIs (analyzers, .NET Upgrade Assistant).
4. Replace what is missing: WCF server, Remoting, Web Forms.
5. Switch the app to net10.0 and run the tests.
cards/5/q: Put the migration steps in order
cards/5/explain: A shared standard library lets you migrate piece by piece.
cards/6/q: What will you have to replace when leaving Framework? Select all that apply.
cards/6/explain: LINQ and async are available everywhere.
cards/7/q: Can you write C# 12 for net48?
cards/7/options/0: Much of the syntax compiles, but only C# 7.3 is officially supported, and features that need new APIs or runtime support will not work
cards/7/explain: Default interface methods, for example, need runtime support, and Framework does not have it.
